passage: Tutor's note. In Tuesday's video seminar Vinita went silent for nearly a minute after I asked a question about the reading. Her camera stayed on, but her eyes moved to a corner of the screen and she did not unmute. In a physical room I would have read the frown as confusion, but online it could also have been a slow connection or a distraction at home. I typed in the chat, "Vinita, no rush. Do you want me to rephrase, or would you like to think and type your answer?" She unmuted and said the audio had lagged and that she'd also been unsure of one term. I explained the term. Tejas, another student, added a quick example. I will use direct check-ins more often on video.

passage: Tuesday, 9 pm. Today's video call was a mess. I'm Nandini and I got confused about the group task, but every time I tried to speak, the lag made me talk over Sunaina. So I stayed muted and looked at my notes, hoping it would sort itself out. Sunaina, I think, read my frozen face as boredom. She said, "Nandini, you okay? You've gone quiet." I typed in the chat that I was lost about step three. She slowed down and explained. I felt so relieved that I nearly cried, which is silly. Note to self: say out loud when I'm stuck, and put it in the chat if the audio is bad. Nobody can see my head from there.
